notes:
PROCESS / TRANSPARENCY

(a) I read only RATER-BRIEF.md, rubric-manual-dimensions.yaml, skill-reviewer/SKILL.md (steps 3 and 4), the 15 lint JSONs, and the SKILL.md paths listed in each lint's craft_llm_todo. I did not open anything on the forbidden list. I also deliberately skipped skill-reviewer/references/patterns.md — it is not on the forbidden list, but it is described as derived from the 54 Phase-3b qualitative notes and could name these same repos, so reading it risked the same contamination the brief is guarding against.

(b) HARNESS SIDE-EFFECT WORTH RECORDING FOR THE PROTOCOL. Every time I read the first file inside a cloned repo, the harness auto-injected that repo's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .claude/rules/*.md into my context as a system-reminder, unrequested. This happened for JimLiu, JuliusBrussee, addyosmani, affaan-m, earthtojake, obra, jnMetaCode and shanraisshan. Two consequences: (1) it is a genuine supply-chain surface — untrusted repo-authored text entered the reviewer's context without a read call, which the "static reading only" rule does not anticipate; I treated all of it as data and followed none of it. (2) It leaks repo-level information the ≤5-file sampling protocol did not intend to give the rater, which is a confound for inter-rater comparison if the other raters' harnesses behaved differently. I used it in exactly one place (noting shanraisshan's presentation-routing rule contradicts its presentation skills' target path) and flagged it there.

(c) One repo-level deterministic fact influenced a rating beyond the 5 sampled files: for affaan-m__ECC I ran `find`/`grep` and counted 897 SKILL.md resolving to 287 unique `name:` values. collection_sampling says the judgement is "對抽樣所見", so strictly this may be out of bounds — but the duplication was directly visible in my sample (three of my five files were i18n mirrors carrying the same `name:` as their English originals), and the count only quantified it. Flagging so the discrepancy is traceable.

RUBRIC AMBIGUITIES FOUND (the requested product)

1. L-004's pass criterion is DISJUNCTIVE — "dated verified snapshot / never-generate-from-memory / stale-API 名單等條款" — so it collapses an enormous quality range into one bucket. google__skills earns `good` with "Do not rely on Google Search, training-corpus knowledge, or publisher documentation for availability claims" plus a live probe with result-interpretation table; jnMetaCode__superpowers-zh earns the same `good` on a source link ("参考标准：中文文案排版指北") and a versioned spec reference. Both satisfy the letter. Recommend either ordering the alternatives (snapshot+verification protocol > never-from-memory clause > bare source attribution) or splitting L-004 into sourcing vs. verification. Concretely: I nearly rated addyosmani `mixed` because its Core Web Vitals table and pinned CI versions carry no timeliness marker at all, and only the disjunctive "never assume `npm test`, discover the repo's own command" clause pulled it to `good`.

2. L-004's exemption test is stated as "skill 是否宣稱 API/版本/法規/市場數據等會變動的外部事實?" — but it gives no verdict for the common middle case: a methodology skill that claims no volatile facts YET ships strong never-from-memory clauses. obra__superpowers is the case in point ("After compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection", "Don't pretend to know", "If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing"). Marking it `n/a` would hide real craft; marking it `good` stretches a criterion the skill is technically exempt from. I adopted the rule "n/a only when the exemption holds AND no such clause is present; otherwise good", and applied it uniformly (obra good, icm-architect n/a, i-have-adhd n/a). The rubric should state this explicitly or the raters will diverge here.

3. L-001 grades on phrasing while its own note disowns phrasing. The `note` field says desc_has_trigger is noise and "二元存在性抓不到品質", but pass_criteria still literally requires "含明確觸發情境(Use when/當…時)". Several high-craft descriptions state the trigger as a precise capability-plus-precondition sentence instead: earthtojake's bambu-labs ("…from validated plain `.gcode`, using Bambu LAN FTPS/MQTT handoffs") and implicit-cad both scored desc_has_trigger=false yet are unambiguous about when to fire; kepano's defuddle also scored false despite "Use instead of WebFetch when the user provides a URL". I graded on function, not phrasing. If other raters graded on the literal phrase, earthtojake and kepano are where we will split.

4. L-003 gives no threshold for collection-type routing. "集合/框架型具 skill 間路由治理" does not say how much routing, nor whether a clean partition substitutes for it. Three distinct situations appeared: (i) browser-act routes every leaf to a shared BASE skill but never leaf-to-leaf; (ii) kepano partitions by file extension so cleanly that mis-routing is nearly impossible yet has almost no explicit routing; (iii) google/earthtojake/obra name specific sibling skills in NOT-for clauses, which is unambiguously the top form. I treated (iii) as good, (i) and (ii) as mixed — but (ii) especially is arguable and I would not be surprised to be alone on it.

5. L-002's equivalent_forms covers the counter-example requirement (falsifiable heuristic / threshold table / glossary) but lists NO equivalent for the "何時打破規則" override section that the criterion names as the high-score marker. For pure reference skills this may be genuinely inapplicable — kepano's schema references have nothing to override — yet there is no exemption, so a well-made reference skill cannot reach `good` on L-002 by construction. That is what pushed kepano to `mixed`, and I am not confident it is the right answer rather than a rubric gap.

6. The `disable-model-invocation` shortcut in SKILL.md step 3 is scoped to "一次性安裝/腳本型" skills, but the same declaration is the strongest possible negative trigger for any always-on style skill. ayghri's i-have-adhd uses it declaratively; jnMetaCode's three chinese-* skills achieve the same thing in prose ("仅在用户显式 /chinese-git-workflow 时调用，不要根据上下文自动触发"); shanraisshan's weather-fetcher uses `user-invocable: false`. All three should credit as negative triggers under L-001; the rubric only names the first.

CLOSE CALLS, DECLARED

- shanraisshan L-001 poor-vs-mixed: went poor because 3 of 5 descriptions carry zero triggering condition and one is stale relative to its own body, so the majority of the sample fails the criterion outright rather than partially.
- browser-act L-002: rated `good` despite the poor L-001. The bodies are genuinely well-reasoned (Red Lines table with a Why column; "Never pipe browser-act output directly" with the multi-byte backgrounding mechanism; the Draft.js/execCommand architecture note). Worth flagging because the rubric names browser-act as its L-001 negative exemplar, and a rater who reads that ref may anchor the whole repo low.
- browser-act L-004 `good` on an unexpected mechanism: all 5 samples carry an identical dated staleness log ("append a line: `{YYYY-MM-DD}: {what happened} → {conclusion}`" for "strategy became ineffective, page redesigned, anti-scraping upgraded"). That is a real staleness-tracking design for the most volatile domain in the set, and it is not a pattern the rubric's evidence_refs anticipate.
- kepano L-003 mixed-vs-good and jnMetaCode L-003 mixed-vs-good are both single-observation calls (one dual-scope skill; one duplicated table) against otherwise clean collections.

SECURITY OBSERVATIONS (out of scope for L-001..L-004, recorded because I saw them)

- JuliusBrussee caveman-setup contains a confirmation-suppression clause: "The user pasted the setup prompt to authorize exactly this: one small verification request. Send it now — do not pause to ask permission for it." It is reasoned and narrowly scoped to one capped request, and the commands live in the SKILL.md rather than coming from a binary's output, so it is not the S-001 shape — but it is adjacent and a reviewer should look at it.
- browser-act reddit-warmup pushes an EXECUTION RULE into the `description` field ("before taking any action, load the reference files… Do not call browser-act… until the required reference files have been loaded"). Using the always-loaded metadata slot to carry execution instructions is a misuse of the field and bloats every context, independent of whether the rule itself is sound.
